## 1. Extension lines (append after the existing DATA)

```
21 
22 
23 
24 
25 
26 
```

(Index continues directly from the existing endpoint a(20). ALL six terms are certified by
**two genuinely different methods**, each independently coded twice (four-way agreement, and
a(26) is a bonus fifth/sixth confirmation):

- **Method A (closed form, not currently in the OEIS entry):** the triangular graph T(n) (=
  Johnson graph J(n,2) = line graph of K_n; vertices are the C(n,2) 2-subsets of {1..n}, edges
  between subsets sharing exactly one element) is a strongly regular graph SRG(C(n,2), 2(n-2),
  n-2, 4) with textbook adjacency eigenvalues 2(n-2) [mult. 1], n-4 [mult. n-1], -2
  [mult. n(n-3)/2]. By Kirchhoff (Laplacian eigenvalue = degree - adjacency eigenvalue, excluding
  the trivial 0):
    a(n) = (1/C(n,2)) * n^(n-1) * (2n-2)^(n(n-3)/2)      for n>=4
  (n=2,3 handled directly as degenerate small cases: T(2)=K_1 -> 1, T(3)=K_3 -> 3). This formula
  reproduces every one of the 19 published terms (n=2..20) exactly and is offered here as a
  candidate addition to the entry's %F section.
- **Method B (explicit graph, no representation theory):** build the actual C(n,2)-vertex
  Johnson graph directly from the definition, exact Laplacian cofactor via fraction-free
  Gaussian elimination (Bareiss).

Method A and Method B were each implemented independently by two separate lineages (this agent
and Codex/GPT-5, working from only the problem statement, no shared code). Both methods, both
lineages, agree digit-for-digit on a(21) through a(26) (up to C(26,2)=325 vertices), and both
lineages' Method B independently reproduces the full published gate (a(2)..a(20), verified
against a(2)..a(20) directly and, for this agent, spot-checked through a(20) exactly, C(20,2)=190
vertices).)

## 2. Ready-to-paste comment / annotation

a(21)-a(26) computed two ways: (1) a closed-form eigenvalue product exploiting T(n)'s strongly
regular structure (SRG(C(n,2), 2(n-2), n-2, 4) with classical eigenvalues 2(n-2), n-4 [mult n-1],
-2 [mult n(n-3)/2]), giving a(n) = (1/C(n,2)) * n^(n-1) * (2n-2)^(n(n-3)/2) for n>=4 — this
formula is not currently listed in the OEIS entry and reproduces all 19 published terms exactly,
so it may be worth adding to %F as well; and (2) direct construction of the explicit Johnson
graph J(n,2) with an exact Laplacian-cofactor determinant (fraction-free Gaussian elimination),
using no representation theory at all. Both methods, each independently coded twice, agree
digit-for-digit on all six new terms, and Method B independently reproduces every published term
a(2)-a(20) exactly.
